title: Performance Analysis of Scientific Applications on an NVIDIA Grace System
problem: Frontera is reaching end-of-life and requires replacement, but the successor Horizon is not yet available. Vista serves as an intermediate system using new NVIDIA Grace processors that need performance characterization on existing scientific HPC workloads.
motivation: Understanding how new processor architectures perform on traditional HPC applications is critical for informing system procurement decisions and enabling researchers to effectively use intermediate systems.
method: Researchers tested NVIDIA's new Grace processors on Vista by running real scientific applications on them. They compared the performance directly against Intel and AMD processors running the same applications at TACC (the Texas Advanced Computing Center). By measuring actual workloads instead of synthetic benchmarks, they got the first reliable picture of how Grace performs for the kinds of scientific computing that researchers actually do.
key_novelty: This work provides the first performance measurements of NVIDIA's Grace CPU architecture when running real scientific HPC (high-performance computing) applications on an academic supercomputer.
contributions: Early performance evaluation of Grace-Grace processor on key scientific applications
Comparative performance analysis between Grace, Intel, and AMD processors at TACC
Design and architecture documentation of the Vista intermediate system
Performance baseline data for assessing Grace viability in HPC environments
limitations: Limited to Grace-Grace CPU performance only; Grace-Hopper GPU component performance deferred to future work.
primary_theme: Grace CPU performance characterization for HPC
